subsystems.name: Population microdata layer
subsystems.role: a statistical picture of who lives in the jurisdiction: age, income, location, employment, health, mobility.

subsystems.name: Agent population
subsystems.role: millions of synthetic individuals whose joint statistics match the real population.

subsystems.name: Behavioural engine
subsystems.role: decides what each agent does when the rules change.
parts: language-model personas for reasoning and messaging
calibrated response parameters from past policy changes

subsystems.name: Environment model
subsystems.role: the world agents act in: labour and housing markets, prices, transport, public services.

subsystems.name: Law-injection and scenario layer
subsystems.role: translates a drafted law into changed parameters and rules the agents feel.

subsystems.name: Validation and uncertainty layer
subsystems.role: tests whether the simulation reproduces outcomes we already know, and reports the range.

subsystems.name: Audit and governance layer
subsystems.role: keeps the tool honest and inspectable.

buildSteps.title: Define the question and the baseline
buildSteps.detail: Specify which outcomes matter — employment, cost of living, small-business survival — and build a no-change baseline to compare against.

buildSteps.title: Assemble microdata
buildSteps.detail: Combine census, survey and administrative records under privacy safeguards to get a statistically faithful starting population.

buildSteps.title: Generate the synthetic population
buildSteps.detail: Sample millions of agents so that aggregate statistics match reality, then link them into households, firms and social networks.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate behaviour
buildSteps.detail: Fit response rules to natural experiments and past reforms, so agents react the way real people and firms measurably did.

buildSteps.title: Encode the environment
buildSteps.detail: Implement prices, markets and public services so agents compete for jobs, housing and goods rather than acting in isolation.

buildSteps.title: Translate the drafted law
buildSteps.detail: Convert legal text into explicit parameters — thresholds, rates, eligibility — and record every interpretation as an assumption.

buildSteps.title: Run the ensemble
buildSteps.detail: Run the scenario many times with varied assumptions and random seeds, then publish distributions rather than a single number.

buildSteps.title: Back-test and stress-test
buildSteps.detail: Replay historical laws the model never saw and check whether it would have predicted the observed outcome.

buildSteps.title: Report, publish and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Release results with error bars and assumptions; feed the disagreements between model and reality back into recalibration.

prerequisites.why: economic and epidemic agent models exist and are used, but they rarely capture a whole society's response.
needed to give agents plausible reasoning, speech and heterogeneous reactions.
accuracy depends on detailed population data, much of which is restricted, sparse or not collected.
counterfactuals can never be directly observed, so predictive skill has to be inferred indirectly.
millions of agents over many runs need heavy compute while protecting personal data.

pathway.milestone: agent-based models used for specific questions such as disease spread, tax changes or transport demand
pathway.unlocks: narrow, testable simulation of one policy lever at a time.

pathway.milestone: language-model personas reproduce survey and voting responses at population level
pathway.unlocks: richer representation of opinion, messaging and behavioural heterogeneity.

pathway.milestone: retrospective validation: models reproduce the measured effects of past reforms across several countries
pathway.unlocks: justified use as one input in impact assessment, alongside cost-benefit analysis.

pathway.milestone: institutional use as a documented, audited advisory tool with mandatory uncertainty reporting
pathway.unlocks: faster, cheaper pre-testing of draft laws — while keeping the final decision with elected people.

pathway.milestone: continuously updated national digital twins that regulators query in real time
pathway.unlocks: adaptive regulation that is revised as evidence accumulates rather than years later.
